attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 910.121 ms, failures 0

report.summary: Outbox publication fell to ~10/10s against 22/10s arrivals, building a backlog (pending up to 200). Consumer handler latency (p95 ~910ms) is the likely limiter; the serial-delivery link is not confirmed.

findings.claim: Publications lagged arrivals: 510 published vs 592 committed, with per-bucket publications ~10 vs 22 arrivals for most of the window, then a catch-up burst (81, 81).
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show a sustained throughput deficit and pending rising 1 to 157, matching late notifications.

findings.claim: Deliveries did not fail. All 509 attempts succeeded with status 200, with no auth, server or network errors. The slowness is in the consumer handler (p95 ~910ms vs p50 0.016ms).
findings.reason: Outcome counts are all success. Handler time accounts for the tail, while auth is ~70ms and unattributed time is ~1ms.

findings.claim: The slow consumer handler plausibly throttled the outbox poller (batch 20, 1s poll) and so caused the backlog. DB or pool contention is not involved.
findings.reason: Pool and DB show no waiting, and the config is batch 20 at 1s, so the slow tail is the remaining candidate for the rate drop.

limitations: No per-time-bucket correlation of slow handler attempts with the publication dips, and no view of whether the poller delivers serially.
Handler timings come from the fixture consumer, and the cause of the 296 old FAILED rows is not visible.
next_checks: Correlate slow-handler attempts by timestamp with the low-publication buckets, and check the poller's delivery concurrency.
Inspect the 296 FAILED outbox rows (last error, attempts) and decide whether to requeue them.

alternatives.reason: The failed count stayed at 296 and predates the window, so it does not explain the in-window backlog growth, though those messages stay undelivered.
alternatives.hypothesis: The 296 FAILED outbox rows (static, age ~5550s+) are the cause of the late notifications.

alternatives.reason: No pool waits or timeouts, and no blocking sessions in 120 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: DB or connection pool contention slowed publication.
